questions.questionText: How many phases are there in the lifecycle of a ReactJS component?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Four.

questions.questionText: Which are the phases of the ReactJS component lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Initialization, Mounting, Updating, Unmounting.

questions.questionText: In which phase are the props and state of the component set up?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Initialization.

questions.questionText: In which phase are the DOM elements of the component created and rendered so that they become visible to the user?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Mounting.

questions.questionText: A component is in the updating phase when:
options: It is removed from the DOM
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Its props or state change.

questions.questionText: In which phase are the DOM elements associated with a component destroyed?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Unmounting.

questions.questionText: Why was handling lifecycle phases with class component methods considered cumbersome?
options: Many methods were rarely used and hard to remember for beginners
questions.correctAnswer: Many methods were rarely used and hard to remember for beginners
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Many methods were rarely used and hard to remember for beginners.

questions.questionText: Which single hook can solve the lifecycle needs in functional components?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) useEffect.

questions.questionText: How many arguments does the useEffect hook take?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Two.

questions.questionText: What are the two arguments of useEffect?
options: A callback function and a dependency array
questions.correctAnswer: A callback function and a dependency array
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) A callback function and a dependency array.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct syntax of useEffect?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) useEffect(callback function, dependency array);.

questions.questionText: What decides which phase of the component useEffect handles?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) The dependency array.

questions.questionText: When is the callback called in useEffect(() => {}, [])?
options: Only once, when the component is mounted
questions.correctAnswer: Only once, when the component is mounted
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Only once, when the component is mounted.

questions.questionText: What does an empty dependency array in useEffect handle?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) The mounting phase.

questions.questionText: When is the callback called if no dependency array is given to useEffect?
options: Whenever any state or props change in the component
questions.correctAnswer: Whenever any state or props change in the component
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Whenever any state or props change in the component.

questions.questionText: When no dependency array is given, the component is in which phase when the callback runs?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Updating.

questions.questionText: In useEffect(() => {}, [v1, v2]), when is the callback called?
options: Only when v1 or v2 changes (and on mount)
questions.correctAnswer: Only when v1 or v2 changes (and on mount)
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Only when v1 or v2 changes (and on mount).

questions.questionText: Where can clean-up code be written inside useEffect?
options: In the function returned from the callback
questions.correctAnswer: In the function returned from the callback
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) In the function returned from the callback.

questions.questionText: When is the function returned by the useEffect callback executed?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) When the component starts unmounting.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of clean-up code in useEffect?
options: Destroying variables and resources no longer needed, preventing memory leaks
questions.correctAnswer: Destroying variables and resources no longer needed, preventing memory leaks
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Destroying variables and resources no longer needed, preventing memory leaks.

questions.questionText: Values in the dependency array are given to write clean-up code in useEffect. This statement is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) False.

questions.questionText: When no dependency array is given, the component will be in the updating phase when either props or state changes. This statement is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) True.

questions.questionText: Which feature introduced in React v18 renders every component twice in development to ensure there are no errors?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) StrictMode.

questions.questionText: In which environment do effects run twice due to StrictMode?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Development only.

questions.questionText: When the code reaches users in production, how many times do components run their setup?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Once.

questions.questionText: In which file can StrictMode be commented out to test without it?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) index.js.

questions.questionText: In Code Snippet 3 (no dependency array), when does the console log run?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Whenever like or dislike changes.

questions.questionText: In Code Snippet 4 with [like] as the dependency array, when does the callback run?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Only when like changes.

questions.questionText: In the Timer example with useEffect(() => {...}, []), why does "useEffect runs" print only once?
options: The empty dependency array runs the callback only on mounting
questions.correctAnswer: The empty dependency array runs the callback only on mounting
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) The empty dependency array runs the callback only on mounting.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to start the interval in the Timer example?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) setInterval.

questions.questionText: Which function is used in the clean-up code to stop the interval?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) clearInterval.

questions.questionText: In setTime((prev) => prev + 1), what is prev?
options: The previous value of time passed to the callback
questions.correctAnswer: The previous value of time passed to the callback
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) The previous value of time passed to the callback.

questions.questionText: setTime accepts:
options: Not only values but also a callback function
questions.correctAnswer: Not only values but also a callback function
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Not only values but also a callback function.

questions.questionText: What technique is used in {show ? <Timer /> : null}?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Conditional Rendering.

questions.questionText: When show is false in conditional rendering, what happens to <Timer />?
options: It is hidden but kept mounted
It is removed from the DOM
questions.correctAnswer: It is removed from the DOM
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) It is removed from the DOM.

questions.questionText: Why does "Timer called" keep printing after the Timer component is removed (without clean-up)?
options: A memory leak: the interval did not stop
questions.correctAnswer: A memory leak: the interval did not stop
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) A memory leak: the interval did not stop.

questions.questionText: How is the memory leak in the Timer example solved?
options: Using clearInterval in the return function of useEffect
questions.correctAnswer: Using clearInterval in the return function of useEffect
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Using clearInterval in the return function of useEffect.

questions.questionText: What message is printed when the Timer is stopped in Code Snippet 7?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Timer stopped.

questions.questionText: What does the useEffect hook generally synchronize ReactJS components with?
options: External systems such as fetching data from an API
questions.correctAnswer: External systems such as fetching data from an API
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) External systems such as fetching data from an API.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about memory leaks?
options: They need to be handled in the clean-up part of useEffect
questions.correctAnswer: They need to be handled in the clean-up part of useEffect
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) They need to be handled in the clean-up part of useEffect.

questions.questionText: Which phase is the component in when the empty dependency array's callback is called?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Mounting.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes the dependency array containing multiple values?
options: There can be n number of values
questions.correctAnswer: There can be n number of values
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) There can be n number of values.

questions.questionText: Mostly, the values in a dependency array are:
options: State or props of the component
questions.correctAnswer: State or props of the component
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) State or props of the component.

questions.questionText: The lifecycle of ReactJS components is compared in the session to:
options: Human life phases from birth to death
questions.correctAnswer: Human life phases from birth to death
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Human life phases from birth to death.

questions.questionText: Which hook is used together with setInterval inside the Timer's callback to start the timer when mounted?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) useEffect.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct way to make a callback run once on mount?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) useEffect(() => {}, []);.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct way to make a callback run on every state or props change?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) useEffect(() => {});.

questions.questionText: What does the summary say about the dependency array?
options: It dictates in which phase the callback function will be called
questions.correctAnswer: It dictates in which phase the callback function will be called
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) It dictates in which phase the callback function will be called.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a lifecycle phase of ReactJS components?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Compiling.
